deals.evidence: The New York Yankees will receive a $2.6 billion financing injection from Apollo Global Management
deals.headline: Apollo agrees $2.6bn debt-and-equity injection into Yankee Global Enterprises
deals.seller: Steinbrenner family and some limited partners
deals.summary: Apollo provides a combination of debt and equity to YGE, refinancing existing debt and taking a minority stake of undisclosed value; the Steinbrenners stay full control owners. Sportico later reported the family sold at least 4% of YGE in the deal and that it valued YGE at more than $10bn (sources). Apollo Sports Capital CEO Al Tylis joins the YGE board.

name: New York Yankees
notes: Revenue, operating income and player expenses are Forbes estimates for the 2025 season (Forbes: revenue net of stadium revenues used for debt payments; Debt/Value 1%). Sportico's March 2026 valuation is $9.4bn incl. YES Network and related businesses ('The New York Yankees are No. 1 for the sixth straight year at $9.4 billion'). Apollo's exact stake is not stated by Sportico (MLB caps a single fund at 15%); press reports of a 16% stake and of the family keeping 'a bit more than 60%' come from outlets not citable here. YGE also holds ~10% of AC Milan, 10% of NYCFC, ~16% of Legends and 26% of YES Network (Sportico, July 2026). Stadium owner, social counts and attendance not found on a citable page.

ownership_summary: The Steinbrenner family has controlled the Yankees since George Steinbrenner led a group that bought the club in 1973 for $8.8m; the parent company is Yankee Global Enterprises (YGE), which also holds stakes in AC Milan, NYCFC, Legends and the YES Network. In August 2026 Apollo agreed a $2.6bn debt-and-equity injection into YGE, taking a minority stake (the Steinbrenners and some LPs sold shares; deal valued YGE at more than $10bn per Sportico's sources); the family remains full control owner.
